const isClassExtendsClause = (node: any, parent: any): boolean =>
  (isClassDeclaration(parent) || isClassExpression(parent)) &&
  parent.superClass === node;

const hasPostfixPart = (node: any, parent: any) =>
  ((isMemberExpression(parent) || isOptionalMemberExpression(parent)) &&
    parent.object === node) ||
  ((isCallExpression(parent) ||
    isOptionalCallExpression(parent) ||
    isNewExpression(parent)) &&
    parent.callee === node) ||
  (isTaggedTemplateExpression(parent) && parent.tag === node) ||
  isTSNonNullExpression(parent);

export function NullableTypeAnnotation(node: any, parent: any): boolean {
  return isArrayTypeAnnotation(parent);
}

content.text:
I fixed the bug in Babel's code generator. When the arrow function is converted to a regular function, the output was `function () {...}().map(c, v0).map++;` with no wrapping parentheses. A statement that starts with `function` is read as a function declaration, and a declaration needs a name, hence the error. It now prints `(function () {...})().map(c, v0).map++;`.

**Cause:** in `packages/babel-generator/src/node/parentheses.ts`, the generator decides whether an expression sits at the very start of a statement by walking up through its parent expressions. It already walked up through calls, property access, binary and assignment expressions, but not through a postfix `x++` / `x--`. Since `++` comes after its operand, that operand starts the statement, but the generator stopped checking and left the parentheses off.

**Fix:** postfix update expressions are now part of that walk. Prefix ones (`++x`) are unchanged, because the `++` already comes first.

**Verified:** after rebuilding, a small script that builds the syntax tree directly now generates `(function () {})().map++;`, and the prefix form is still `++function () {}().map;`. The existing generator test suite passes (532 passed, 4 skipped). I did not run the full preset-env and transform-runtime setup from the issue, and I didn't add a new test case.
